sourceDistinctions: Kamstra’s awakened Beast has Small size and speaks Common. Pack Tactics requires a bonus action and covers only the next qualifying attack this turn.
The trait box explicitly grants finesse for Sneak Attack. This build wears no armor and does not rely on carried tools.

Use the 2014 fighter and Soldier background. The printed appendage has no special reach.

entries.name: Cyclopian

entries.aliases: Cyclopian / cyclopians. Use the knowledge-eating humanoid's traits. Keep the independent Cyclops conversion separate.

source.name: Cyclopian
source.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
source.publisher: Loot Tavern and Hit Point Press
source.author: Loot Tavern design team
source.version: First-printing chapter 6, read from the rendered original page
source.heading: Cyclopian Traits
sourceDistinctions: The written creature type is Humanoid plus the stated Aberration qualification.
AC 12 assumes no spell slot has been spent. Mage armor gives AC 15 for eight hours.

entries.name: Dara
entries.publication: Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass (5.5e )
entries.aliases: Dara. Keep the core 5.5e printing distinct from the 2014 version and later Yatamon options.

source.name: Dara
source.publication: Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass (5.5e )
source.author: Adam Lee, Ari Levitch, and Jeremiah Crofton
source.version: 5.5e , ISBN 978-1-954777-16-3, second printing July 2025
source.heading: Dara Traits and Talisman Forms
sourceDistinctions: The printed profile groups Blue and Red Dara. Selka uses Blue. The color text says Blue knows Knowledge and Red knows Might, and says each can produce that form once per day in addition to other forms. The formal trait grants one creation per Long Rest. This build uses a single shared use. The one-hour lifetime comes from the shared creation rule.
Selka can choose any form open to Blue Dara, including Knowledge. Selka has Sacred Revelation immediately. Impart Knowledge begins at level 10.
Read the Talisman Forms table on the rendered original spread. The search index omitted that table.

entries.name: Deepborn
entries.aliases: Deepborn of Olmarsh. This fish-like lineage is separate from Sea Spawn, Gillfolk, and Deep Scion.

source.name: Deepborn
source.heading: Deepborn Traits
source.provenance: Avantris Entertainment's 2024 Player v1.1. Playable species traits for the 2024 fifth-edition rules.

entries.name: Dreamlands Cat
entries.aliases: Dreamlands Cat / Dreamlands Cats. Keep all player options in the same profile. Saturnian and Uranian encounter cat records have their own scopes.

source.name: Dreamlands Cat
source.author: Sandy Petersen, James Jacobs, Arthur Petersen, Ian Starcher, and David N. Ross
source.heading: Dreamlands Cat Traits
source.version: Copyright 2018, ISBN 978-0-9995390-4-0. Author text consulted in a reproduction.
sourceDistinctions: Use the 1d3 days from Nine Lives in the actual trait block. The earlier lore text describes a 4d6-hour return for a mundane cat.
Terran, Martian, Saturnian, and Uranian are printed subraces. The original NPC uses Terran.

entries.name: Enkoh
entries.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
entries.aliases: Enkoh / enkoh. Keep Hulking and Springtail within the same species.

source.name: Enkoh
source.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
source.version: Final v1.00 digital printing, read from its rendered authored folios
source.heading: Enkoh Traits
sourceDistinctions: Toma uses the Hulking form. His +2 Strength and +1 Constitution use the flexible adjustments on p. 117.

entries.name: Flying Snake
entries.aliases: Flying Snake / Flying Snakes. Use the awakened player form. Keep Couatl and Giant Poisonous Snake separate.

source.name: Flying Snake
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: p. 231 in v2. Flying Snake Traits.
source.provenance: Checked against the printed v2 player trait block in the PDFCoffee mirror.
sourceDistinctions: The printed player trait block grants 30-ft. flight and does not include Flyby. The design commentary mentions Flyby but adds no player trait.

V2 p. 7 makes bonus-action monk strikes conventional. Copper Sedge uses a short tail slap for the bonus unarmed strike, with the normal monk die and 5-ft. reach. For the split bite damage, this build adds Dexterity to piercing only.

entries.name: Fuyōren
entries.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
entries.aliases: Fuyōren / Fuyoren. Fuyōhren and Fuyohren are alternate spellings in listings. Aquatic plant folk. Keep Hanamori and other plant species separate.

source.name: Fuyōren
source.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
source.version: Final v1.00 digital printing, read from its rendered authored folios
source.heading: Fuyōren Traits
sourceDistinctions: Fuyōren is the v1.00 trait heading, distinct from the draft and roster spelling Fuyōhren.

entries.name: Giant Centipede
entries.aliases: Giant Centipede / Giant Centipedes. Use the individual awakened player traits. Swarms have separate encounter rules.

source.name: Giant Centipede
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: p. 234 in v2. Giant Centipede Traits.
source.provenance: Checked against the printed v2 player trait block in the PDFCoffee mirror.
sourceDistinctions: The printed player trait block gives blindsight 60 ft. The design commentary mentions 30 ft. This profile follows the trait block.

Damage uses the player’s two dice and can supply a finesse Sneak Attack. The encounter entry’s paralysis rider does not apply. For the split bite damage, this build assigns Dexterity and Sneak Attack to piercing.

entries.name: Giant Eagle
entries.aliases: Giant Eagle / Giant Eagles. Use the printed player species and keep Roc and ordinary eagle profiles separate.

source.name: Giant Eagle
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: p. 235 in v2, Giant Eagle Traits.
source.heading: Giant Eagle Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for 2014 fifth edition, using the v2 printed traits.
sourceDistinctions: The printed flight trait gives 60 ft. The 80 ft. figure in the design notes on p. 236 does not govern this profile.

entries.name: Giant Frog
entries.aliases: Giant Frog / Giant Frogs. Use the awakened beast profile. Froghemoth, Bullywug, and Nakudama remain separate.

source.name: Giant Frog
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: pp. 236–237 in v2, Giant Frog Traits.
source.heading: Giant Frog Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for 2014 fifth edition, using the v2 printed traits.
sourceDistinctions: The heading starts on p. 236. The trait continuation on p. 237 grants neither Standing Leap nor Darkvision, despite both being named in the design notes.

Silt uses the bite as the physical grip for the species' bonus-action grapple. The ordinary size limit, reach, and Athletics contest still apply. Dexterity can govern the bite, while the grapple still uses Strength.

entries.name: Giant Hyena
entries.aliases: Giant Hyena / Giant Hyenas. Use the awakened player profile and keep Gnoll separate.

source.name: Giant Hyena
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: p. 238 in v2, Giant Hyena Traits.
source.heading: Giant Hyena Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for 2014 fifth edition, using the v2 printed traits.
sourceDistinctions: The printable trait gives 30 ft. walk speed. The design notes discuss 40 ft. and suggest Pack Tactics as an optional change. Neither applies to the printed player profile.

entries.name: Giant Octopus
entries.aliases: Giant Octopus / Giant Octopuses. Use the awakened beast package. Pode and other octopus folk retain their own rules.

source.name: Giant Octopus
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: pp. 239–240 in v2, Giant Octopus Traits.
source.heading: Giant Octopus Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player conversion for 2014 fifth edition, using the v2 printed traits.
sourceDistinctions: The published trait includes no automatic grab or restraint rider on the tentacle attack, although the design notes discuss Grab.
Ink Cloud omits its activation timing. Dunewick uses an action for the release as a table ruling, consistent with the encounter ability that inspired it.
For Martial Arts, Kamstra's p. 7 uses the monk damage die for the bonus-action strike rather than the species' larger natural damage die.

entries.name: Giant Owl
entries.aliases: Giant Owl / Giant Owls. Use the individual awakened player profile, separate from Hsiao and owl-like humanoids.

source.name: Giant Owl
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player rules for 2014 fifth edition, using the v2 printing.
sourceDistinctions: The player traits start on p. 240; Talons and Languages continue on p. 241. This owl is naturally intelligent per the play advice.
The No Hands line forbids weapons and shields, then refers to tentacles. Reedwatch uses no manual equipment. Its talons can scratch the mud without assuming tool use.
Flyby is a bonus-action Disengage in this printing. Talons explicitly count as finesse for Sneak Attack.

entries.name: Giant Poisonous Snake
entries.aliases: Giant Poisonous Snake / Giant Venomous Snake as a descriptive name. Preserve the printed player venom and handling limits.

source.name: Giant Poisonous Snake
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.page: v2 p. 241, Giant Poisonous Snake Traits
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player rules for 2014 fifth edition, using the v2 printing.
sourceDistinctions: The player Bite adds a poison die on a hit without a separate saving throw. The 1d4 damage dice are not imported from an encounter block.
Kamstra’s p. 7 Monk exception limits the bonus strike to conventional bludgeoning rather than Bite. The primary Attack action keeps its printed Bite.

entries.name: Giant Spider
entries.aliases: Giant Spider / Giant Spiders. Use the awakened player profile. Spiderfolk, Silkborn, and Phase Spider remain separate.

source.name: Giant Spider
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player rules for 2014 fifth edition, using the v2 printing.
sourceDistinctions: The traits give no attack proficiency rule for Web. Loomstep treats it as a proficient natural ranged attack and uses Dexterity for the roll. The printed escape DC uses Constitution.

Restrained ends when the creature escapes with the stated Strength check or the web is destroyed. The player trait gives no recharge. The table uses one action per use under the normal Attack action rules.

entries.name: Giant Wasp
entries.aliases: Giant Wasp / Giant Wasps. Use the awakened player beast and keep wasp-like lineages and swarms separate.

source.name: Giant Wasp
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Tyler Kamstra's DMs Guild player rules for 2014 fifth edition, using the v2 printing.
sourceDistinctions: This player Sting has no Constitution save, stabilization, or paralysis rider.
Cinderwing uses Strength for Rage damage. The optional extra proficiency or feat mentioned in design commentary is not part of the printed trait block.

entries.name: Gnarlborn
entries.aliases: Gnarlborn. The elderwood folk are separate from Wood Woad, Dryadborn, and other plant species.

source.name: Gnarlborn
source.page: p. 8 in 2024 Player v1.1, Gnarlborn Traits.
source.heading: Gnarlborn Traits
source.provenance: Avantris Entertainment, The Crooked Moon Player for 2024 rules, v1.1.

entries.name: Gnorri
entries.aliases: Gnorri. Use its printed player traits and aquatic requirements. Keep other aquatic profiles separate.

source.name: Gnorri
source.author: Sandy Petersen, James Jacobs, Arthur Petersen, Ian Starcher, and David N. Ross
source.heading: Gnorri Traits
source.version: Copyright 2018, ISBN 978-0-9995390-4-0. Author text consulted in a reproduction.
sourceDistinctions: Seln uses the Blue subrace, two arms, and Gnorri Science, with no Builder Magic. The Large creature handles a Medium spear.

entries.name: Gobboc
entries.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
entries.aliases: Gobboc / gobbocs. Use the printed chicken-like lineage. Goblin and Kenku remain separate.

source.name: Gobboc
source.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
source.publisher: Loot Tavern and Hit Point Press
source.author: Loot Tavern design team
source.version: First-printing chapter 6, read from the rendered original page
source.heading: Gobboc Traits
sourceDistinctions: The source art shows a chicken-like feathered humanoid. The chicken is a distinct spell form and its own stat block, not a second ongoing morph.
The printed Coward’s Creed depends on a melee hit. It does not grant the full rogue Cunning Action feature at level 1.

entries.name: Golynn
entries.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
entries.aliases: Golynn. Use the book's burrowing lineage and its own physical traits.

source.name: Golynn
source.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
source.publisher: Loot Tavern and Hit Point Press
source.author: Loot Tavern design team
source.version: First-printing chapter 6, read from the rendered original page
source.heading: Golynn Traits
sourceDistinctions: The printed golynn has a digging feature and no special claw attack.
Daro’s AC uses natural armor and a shield. Dueling applies with the shield because it is not a weapon.

entries.name: Graveborn
entries.aliases: Graveborn of Syndramas. This ghoul-like lineage has its own traits. Mythos Ghoul and other undead keep separate scopes.

source.heading: Graveborn Traits

source.name: Hanamori
source.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
source.version: Final v1.00 digital printing, read from its rendered authored folios
source.heading: Hanamori Traits
sourceDistinctions: Sumi’s +1 Dexterity and +2 Constitution use the flexible adjustments on p. 117. Rugged and Unarmored Defense are distinct choices.

entries.name: Haniwa
entries.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)

source.name: Haniwa
source.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
source.version: Final v1.00 digital printing, read from its rendered authored folios
source.heading: Haniwa Traits
sourceDistinctions: Grave Guardian uses the 2014 sanctuary with the published Player’s Handbook errata. Earthen uppercut appears on p. 281.
The companion uses the 2014 Mastiff statistics with the printed Clay Companion and Soul Shell changes.

entries.aliases: Harvestborn. Use the living harvest construct lineage. Scarecrow has a separate profile.

source.page: p. 10 in 2024 Player v1.1, Harvestborn Traits.
source.heading: Harvestborn Traits

entries.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)

source.name: Isetsu
source.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
source.version: Final v1.00 digital printing, read from its rendered authored folios
source.heading: Isetsu Traits
sourceDistinctions: The printed Waterborne trait gives no swim speed. Brittle Shell adds a temporary bonus to a chosen AC calculation. Fortune Favoured has no rounding direction in its trait text.

entries.name: Kitsune
entries.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
entries.aliases: Kitsune / fox folk as a descriptive term. Keep the printed tail progression with Kitsune. Vulpera and Vulpin have separate rules.

source.name: Kitsune
source.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
source.heading: Kitsune Traits
source.provenance: Loot Tavern, Ryoko's Guide to the Yokai Realms v1.00, chapter 8. This profile uses the final 2014-compatible player rules.
sourceDistinctions: The final p. 131 gives Fey, a 1-hour form with a reaction rider, 60-ft. motion language, and one chosen skill. The beta differs.

entries.name: Lotol
entries.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
entries.aliases: Lotol / salamander-kin as a descriptive term. Group the printed adaptive choices. Keep other amphibian folk separate.

source.name: Lotol
source.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
source.publisher: Loot Tavern and Hit Point Press
source.author: Loot Tavern design team
source.version: First-printing chapter 6, read from the rendered original page
source.heading: Lotol Traits
sourceDistinctions: Adaptive Polymorphism grants two selections. Tavi has water breathing, swimming, and tongue retrieval from the chosen adaptations, with no Shocking Skin or darkvision.
The art depicts gills and mail. Scale mail is equipment, consistent with the written Lotol skin lacking natural scales.

entries.name: Mycelian
entries.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
entries.aliases: Mycelian / mycelians. Use the fungus-and-host rules. Mycelial, Fungi, and Myconid are separate.

source.name: Mycelian
source.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
source.author: Max Wartelle, Mohamed Bellafquih, and Jesse Jackdaw Burns
source.heading: Mycelian Traits
source.sourceVersion: First edition, first printing, April 2023, ISBN 978-1-9990962-8-1
source.provenance: Player traits from chapter 6 of the April 2023 first printing of Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting, using the 2014 fifth-edition rules.
sourceDistinctions: Fen uses a 2014 dwarf host for size, 25-ft. walk, darkvision and Dwarven Resilience. The host does not confer the rest of the dwarf traits.
The first printing’s optional GM latitude is not needed for the assigned build.

entries.name: Mythos Ghoul
entries.aliases: Mythos Ghoul / Ghoul in this source. The living Mythos species is distinct from undead encounter ghouls and Avantris Graveborn.

source.name: Mythos Ghoul
source.author: Sandy Petersen, James Jacobs, Arthur Petersen, Ian Starcher, and David N. Ross
source.heading: Ghoul Traits
source.version: Copyright 2018, ISBN 978-0-9995390-4-0. Author text consulted in a reproduction.
sourceDistinctions: The chapter heading reads Ghoul and uses Mythos ghoul to identify this living player option. It has a different creature type and traits from the undead Ghoul encounter record.
The original NPC uses Raised by Ghouls.

entries.name: Nakudama
entries.publication: Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass (5.5e )
entries.aliases: Nakudama / Obojima frog folk as a descriptive term. Use the core 5.5e species, separate from Bullywug and Grung.

source.name: Nakudama
source.publication: Obojima: Tales from the Tall Grass (5.5e )
source.author: Adam Lee, Ari Levitch, and Jeremiah Crofton
source.version: 5.5e , ISBN 978-1-954777-16-3, second printing July 2025
source.heading: Naku Naku and Nakudama Traits
sourceDistinctions: The 2024 trait block lists a 30-ft. Speed and no separate Swim Speed. Amphibious governs breathing. Latching Tongue does not move its target or supply a saving throw in this printing.
The target of Grasping Tongue is an object. Only a creature wearing or carrying it makes the save. The example DC is 8 + 2 Strength + 2 proficiency.

entries.name: Ombrask
entries.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
entries.aliases: Ombrask / ombrasks. Group the printed former-race choices. Keep Shadowcast and other shadow lineages separate.

source.name: Ombrask
source.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
source.author: Max Wartelle, Mohamed Bellafquih, and Jesse Jackdaw Burns
source.page: Chapter 6, pp. 165, Ombrask Traits and Former Race Boons.
source.heading: Ombrask Traits and Former Race Boons
source.sourceVersion: First edition, first printing, April 2023, ISBN 978-1-9990962-8-1
source.provenance: Player traits from chapter 6 of the April 2023 first printing of Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting, using the 2014 fifth-edition rules.
sourceDistinctions: Aster uses the Medium former elf and its +1 Intelligence option. The printed entry does not replace the usual Humanoid type.
This build starts with one captured voice and remains below the 5th-level Fade Away threshold.

entries.name: Oniborne
entries.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
entries.aliases: Oniborne / oni descendants. Group Red, Blue, and Green. The published Oni player and encounter profiles have separate rules.

source.name: Oniborne
source.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
source.heading: Oniborne Traits
source.provenance: Loot Tavern, Ryoko's Guide to the Yokai Realms v1.00, chapter 8. This profile uses the final 2014-compatible player rules.
sourceDistinctions: Reading order puts Weeping Magic with Red. It continues the Red list onto p. 134 before the Blue heading. Blue has no spellcasting from lineage.
Red Magical Scavenger uses the final 1-minute or Harvesting check procedure.

entries.name: Oozekin
entries.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
entries.aliases: Oozekin / ooze kin. Use the native printed profile. Oozefolk, Amoeboid, and Plasmoid keep their own rules.

source.name: Oozekin
source.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
source.author: Max Wartelle, Mohamed Bellafquih, and Jesse Jackdaw Burns
source.heading: Oozekin Traits
source.sourceVersion: First edition, first printing, April 2023, ISBN 978-1-9990962-8-1
source.provenance: Player traits from chapter 6 of the April 2023 first printing of Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting, using the 2014 fifth-edition rules.
sourceDistinctions: Rechecked the printed Cube and Puddle actions and the 2014 acid splash, which targets one creature or a close pair rather than a 5-ft. sphere.
The NPC uses a Medium starting size. Its held shield and mace matter for managing free hands.

entries.name: Opteran
entries.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
entries.aliases: Opteran / opterans. Keep all printed subraces under one claim. Other insectile lineages remain separate.

source.name: Opteran
source.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
source.author: Max Wartelle, Mohamed Bellafquih, and Jesse Jackdaw Burns
source.heading: Opteran Traits
source.sourceVersion: First edition, first printing, April 2023, ISBN 978-1-9990962-8-1
source.provenance: Player traits from chapter 6 of the April 2023 first printing of Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting, using the 2014 fifth-edition rules.
sourceDistinctions: Bobbin is a 1st-level larva. The 20-ft. adult flight and loss of String Shot are from the first printing, and neither applies to this build.

entries.name: Plagueborn
entries.aliases: Plagueborn. Use this published rat-like species. Ratling, Rakin, and other rodent folk are separate.

source.name: Plagueborn
source.page: p. 11 in 2024 Player v1.1, Plagueborn Traits.
source.heading: Plagueborn Traits
source.provenance: Avantris Entertainment, The Crooked Moon Player for 2024 rules, v1.1.

entries.name: Rakin
entries.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
entries.aliases: Rakin. Group Posskin, Tanukin, and Urkin. Keep distinct from Ratling and other woodland folk.

source.name: Rakin
source.publication: Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (first printing)
source.author: Max Wartelle, Mohamed Bellafquih, and Jesse Jackdaw Burns
source.page: Chapter 6, pp. 171, 172, 173, Rakin Traits, Urkin, Posskin, and Tanukin.
source.heading: Rakin Traits, Urkin, Posskin, and Tanukin
source.sourceVersion: First edition, first printing, April 2023, ISBN 978-1-9990962-8-1
source.provenance: Player traits from chapter 6 of the April 2023 first printing of Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting, using the 2014 fifth-edition rules.
sourceDistinctions: Posskin Play Dead on p. 172 omits a word. The October 9, 2024 first-printing errata restores the intended casual-glance wording. The 5-ft. Investigation contest is in the first printing.
Tansy uses Posskin and Deception Expertise, which applies to the Constitution (Deception) contest as a Deception check.

entries.name: Relicborn
entries.aliases: Relicborn. Use this skeleton-like reborn species and its printed lineage traits.

source.name: Relicborn
source.version: 2024 Player v1.1, folio printed on the page
source.heading: Relicborn Traits
sourceDistinctions: The 2024 version uses Undead. The character keeps that creature type.
A roll of 20 or higher on the Dance of Death check qualifies for temporary HP. The die roll for temporary HP does not include Constitution or consume the Hit Point Die.

entries.name: Ryokido
entries.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
entries.aliases: Ryokido / Ryōkido. Use the final turtle lineage, also described as a lion turtle in the final text. Keep Tortle separate.

source.name: Ryokido
source.publication: Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms (v1.00)
source.heading: Ryokido Traits
source.provenance: Loot Tavern, Ryoko's Guide to the Yokai Realms v1.00, chapter 8. This profile uses the final 2014-compatible player rules.
sourceDistinctions: The chapter opens on p. 136, which also contains the start of the traits. P. 137 continues them. P. 135 closes Oniborne.
Ryokido is the canonical key from the final chapter. Ryōkido and Lion Turtle are lookup aliases.

entries.name: Shadow
entries.aliases: Shadow / Shadows. Use the undead player conversion. Keep Shade, Shadowcast, and Shadow Mastiff separate.

source.name: Shadow
source.author: Tyler Kamstra
source.provenance: Checked against the printed v2 player trait block in the PDFCoffee mirror.
sourceDistinctions: The playable trait box omits the encounter monster’s ability score loss and shadow creation. It grants poison immunity. Radiant vulnerability and necrotic resistance appear in the design discussion alone.
The Shadow can write and retains ordinary 0 HP rules. Rest healing is allowed under v2 p. 7. The supplement discusses optional repair spells, which this build does not require.

entries.name: Silkborn
entries.aliases: Silkborn. Use Avantris's arachnid lineage. Spiderfolk, Drider, and other spider-based profiles remain separate.

source.name: Silkborn

sourceDistinctions: Bejeweled Carapace applies to the triggering attack alone. The book grants no constant armor formula.
The jeweled familiar description applies at level 3. The level-1 rogue has only the Thaumaturgy cantrip.

source.name: Stoneborn

source.heading: Stoneborn Traits
sourceDistinctions: The fly speed is half the walking speed, 15 ft. for Penn.

Silver Bulwark states when the reaction is available but does not say whether resistance applies to the triggering damage. This build uses the default reaction timing, beginning resistance after the triggering damage. A table can rule otherwise.
The two Argent Gleam options use one common charge per long rest.

sourceDistinctions: Nishikin and Ryūjin share the Tatsumi entry. Moonblessed requires the full number of dice and adds Constitution once. The sample is a white-primary Nishikin with two Hit Dice.

entries.aliases: Threadborn. Use this living doll lineage. Geppettin and other constructs have separate profiles.

source.name: Threadborn
source.version: 2024 Player v1.1, folio printed on the page
source.heading: Threadborn Traits
sourceDistinctions: The no-slot Calm Emotions expands legal targets to all creature types. Casting from a slot uses the standard target restriction.
Sewn Nature affects breathing, food and drink. It gives no exception to sleep requirements.
You’ve Got a Friend is a separate reaction use of Guidance. The character can still cast the cantrip with its normal action without expending a reaction use.
